thread:
anya: quick heads-up — ran the 4-bit q8_0 build of the new draft-13 model with our entropy-gate speculative wrapper. got solid latency wins on code generation but saw a surprising slump on short-form summarization (news headlines slice).

mike: numbers?

anya: p95 token latency down ~28% on code-gen prompts, tail improvements consistent. throughput x1.6 on batching for small requests. however ROUGE-L dropped ~6% on the 1k headline samples. BERTScore down ~0.03.

sasha: did you use the same speculative threshold and fallback policy as the earlier baseline runs?

anya: yes — reused threshold=0.7, fallback after 2 speculative steps. hypothesis: the entropy-gate is allowing early speculative paths that look fine for code (stable token distributions) but for compressive summarization it prefers shorter/safer continuations that hurt overlap metrics.

ben: can you paste the exact wrapper config?

anya: sure:

```
// speculative wrapper config
speculative_enabled: true
entropy_gate: true
gate_threshold: 0.7
speculative_steps: 2
fallback: immediate_on_entropy_cross
quant_backend: q4_0 (per-layer scale)
```

carol: interesting. for summarization we should measure length bias and repetition too. can you dump sample pairs (prompt, baseline, spec) for 20 random fails?

anya: uploading 20 diffs to the shared bucket now — link in thread. highlights: many spec outputs prefer token sequences like "in short," or "overall," and truncate. baseline tends to paraphrase more.

mike: could this be a quantization artifact interacting with predictive early-exit? e.g., rounded logits changing tie-breaks near end-of-sentence tokens?

anya: plausible. I ran a small ablation: same entropy-gate on FP16 model (no quant) + speculative wrapper -> no regression. so quant+spec seems to be the combo.

ben: plan: replicate runs with (A) quant only, no spec, (B) spec only with FP16, (C) quant+spec but lower gate_threshold to 0.55, (D) quant+spec but speculative_steps=1. Also collect token-level KL between baseline logits and spec logits to see divergence.

anya: already queued A/B/C/D on the cluster. rough ETA 3 hours. I'll push a small script to compute per-token KL and a length-bias stat.

carol: for eval protocol, recommend adding these checks:
- dataset slices: headlines (short), abstractive (medium), long-form (>=200 tokens)
- metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, length ratio, repetition_rate (n-gram overlap), code-specific EM for code-gen slice
- decision rule: regress if ROUGE-L drops >3% AND BERTScore drops >0.02 on any slice

sasha: TAG: also track human-preference proxy — pairwise preference model scores on a 500 sample holdout. sometimes overlap metrics fail to capture brevity improvements.

ben: good call. add pairwise model score. Also track token-compute savings per request to weigh cost/quality tradeoff.

anya: dino-bot: started job cluster/jobs/1739456789-entropy-ablation (A/B/C/D). ETA ~3h.

dino-bot: job queued on gpu-pool-4, est runtime 2.8h. logs -> /logs/1739456789/

anya: quick interim: ran a manual check on 50 code-gen prompts — quant+spec is net positive (pass@1 up slightly on dataset we use for benchmarks). so keeping spec for code path makes sense.

eva: question — can we gate speculative decoding by route? e.g., use model.route == "codegen" -> spec_threshold=0.8, else 0.55. That would be an ops-level fallback.

mike: yep, runtime supports per-route policy. we need a config matrix in the console for canaries.

carol: next steps after ablation: if KL shows large divergence early, we should try a "constrained-spec" version: speculative sampling but apply a soft penalty to tokens whose quantized-logit deviation > epsilon. That might keep quality while preserving speed.

anya: noted. I'll add constrained-spec experiment if A/B/C/D indicate too much divergence. Also will produce a short write-up for PMs explaining tradeoffs + suggested per-route defaults.

ben: please also snapshot a few failing examples in /annotations/1739456789 for qualitative review in the weekly eval sync.

anya: will do. thanks all.

sasha: thanks — keep us posted. :thumbsup:
